title: To‘liq mock imtihon: Speaking
goal_uz: Dars oxirida siz uch qismli gapirish imtihonini vaqt bilan to‘liq topshirasiz, javobingizni eng yuqori daraja mezonlari bo‘yicha o‘zingiz baholaysiz, aniq rivojlanish rejasini tuzasiz va hayajonni boshqarishning kamida uchta usulini qo‘llaysiz.

scenes.title: Gapirish imtihoniga xush kelibsiz
board: Full Mock Exam: Speaking
(To‘liq mock imtihon: gapirish)
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda xatosiz yozishni, ya’ni o‘z matningizni tahrir va korrektura qilishni o‘rgandik. Bugun esa yozuvdan ovozga o‘tamiz: to‘liq gapirish imtihonini xuddi haqiqiydek topshiramiz. Dars oxirida siz uch qismli imtihonni vaqt bilan bajarasiz, o‘zingizni eng yuqori mezonlar bo‘yicha baholaysiz va aniq rivojlanish rejasini tuzasiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back. Today is not about learning something new; it is about performing under real conditions, and leaving with a plan.
scenes.say_uz: Xush kelibsiz. Bugun yangi narsa o‘rganish emas, haqiqiy sharoitda chiqish qilish va reja bilan chiqib ketish haqida.

scenes.title: Imtihon tuzilishi
board: Part 1: Interview (~3 min)
Part 2: Long turn (1 min prep + 2 min talk)
Part 3: Discussion (~5 min)
Record yourself. No pausing.
scenes.say_native: Bizning mock imtihon ko‘pgina xalqaro imtihonlarga o‘xshash uch qismdan iborat. Birinchi qism: o‘zingiz haqingizda qisqa suhbat. Ikkinchi qism: bir daqiqa tayyorlanib, ikki daqiqa to‘xtamay gapirasiz. Uchinchi qism: mavhum mavzularda chuqur muhokama. Muhim shart: telefonda o‘zingizni yozib oling va yozuvni to‘xtatmang.
scenes.say: Interview, long turn, discussion. Record every second, and do not stop the recording, whatever happens.
scenes.say_uz: Suhbat, yakka javob, muhokama. Har bir soniyani yozib oling va nima bo‘lsa ham yozuvni to‘xtatmang.

scenes.title: Besh mezon
board: 1 Fluency & coherence
2 Lexical range
3 Grammatical range & accuracy
4 Pronunciation  5 Interaction
scenes.say_native: Imtihonchi sizni bitta umumiy taassurot bilan emas, alohida mezonlar bo‘yicha baholaydi. Biz besh mezondan foydalanamiz: ravonlik va izchillik, lug‘at boyligi, grammatik xilma-xillik va aniqlik, talaffuz hamda muloqot qobiliyati. Turli imtihonlarda nomlari biroz farq qiladi, lekin mohiyati bir xil. O‘zbek o‘quvchilari ko‘pincha faqat grammatikaga e’tibor beradi, holbuki u beshdan bir qism, xolos.
scenes.say: Examiners score separate criteria, not one vague impression. Grammar is only one fifth of the picture.
scenes.say_uz: Imtihonchilar bitta noaniq taassurotni emas, alohida mezonlarni baholaydi. Grammatika rasmning faqat beshdan bir qismi.

scenes.title: Yuqori daraja: ravonlik va lug‘at
board: Fluency: hesitation is about IDEAS, not words
Coherence: ideas linked naturally, not mechanically
Lexis: precise, flexible, idiomatic
(aniq, moslashuvchan, tabiiy)

examples.t: That's a tricky one, actually. Let me think about it from a parent's point of view.
examples.uz: Bu aslida qiyin savol. Keling, ota-ona nuqtai nazaridan o‘ylab ko‘ray.

scenes.say_native: Eng yuqori darajada ravonlik to‘xtovsiz gapirish degani emas. Ona tilida so‘zlashuvchi ham to‘xtaydi, lekin u so‘z qidirib emas, fikr qidirib to‘xtaydi. Izchillik esa “firstly, secondly” kabi mexanik bog‘lovchilar emas, fikrlarning tabiiy ulanishidir. Lug‘atda yuqori daraja kamyob so‘zlar soni bilan emas, aniqlik bilan o‘lchanadi: to‘g‘ri kollokatsiya, nozik ma’no farqi, o‘rinli idioma.
scenes.say: Pause to think about ideas, never to search for words. And choose the precise word, not the impressive one.
scenes.say_uz: Fikr haqida o‘ylash uchun to‘xtang, hech qachon so‘z qidirish uchun emas. Va ta’sirli emas, aniq so‘zni tanlang.

scenes.title: Yuqori daraja: grammatika, talaffuz, muloqot
board: Grammar: full range, used naturally; slips are rare
Pronunciation: stress, rhythm, intonation used with control
Accent is NOT penalised — intelligibility is
Interaction: respond, develop, invite
scenes.say_native: Grammatikada yuqori daraja murakkab tuzilmalarni tabiiy ishlatishni bildiradi: inversiya, shart gaplar, majhul nisbat, modal perfect. Xatolar juda kam va ular ona tilida so‘zlashuvchining tasodifiy xatosiga o‘xshaydi. Talaffuzda o‘zbekcha aksent jarima emas. Baholanadigani: urg‘u, ritm, ohang va tinglovchi qanchalik oson tushunishi. Muloqotda esa suhbatdoshga javob berish, fikrni rivojlantirish va uni suhbatga taklif qilish muhim.
scenes.say: Your accent is not the problem. Unclear stress and flat intonation are. And in a conversation, respond, develop and invite.
scenes.say_uz: Muammo aksentingizda emas. Noaniq urg‘u va tekis ohangda. Suhbatda esa javob bering, rivojlantiring va taklif qiling.

scenes.title: Xato: murakkab so‘z = yuqori ball
board: ✗ The quintessential ubiquity of smartphones is paramount.
✓ Smartphones are everywhere, and that changes how we pay attention.
✗ forced rare words  ✓ precise, natural words
scenes.say_native: Ko‘p tayyorlanuvchilar ro‘yxatdan yodlangan “zo‘r so‘zlar”ni har gapga tiqishtiradi. Natija: gap g‘ayritabiiy, kollokatsiya noto‘g‘ri, ma’no esa xira. Imtihonchi buni darhol sezadi va lug‘at bahosi oshmaydi, aksincha pasayadi. Ikkinchi gap oddiyroq, lekin aniq va o‘ylangan fikrni beradi.
scenes.say: The quintessential ubiquity of smartphones is paramount: clever-sounding, and empty. Smartphones are everywhere, and that changes how we pay attention: precise.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi gap aqlli eshitiladi, lekin bo‘sh. Smartfonlar hamma joyda va bu diqqatimizni o‘zgartiradi: mana bu aniq.

scenes.title: Javoblarni baholang
board: Q: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
A, B or C: which is top level?
What is wrong with the other two?
scenes.say_native: Endi siz imtihonchisiz. Bitta savolga uchta javobni tinglang: A, B va C. Qaysi biri eng yuqori darajaga mos keladi? Qolgan ikkitasining aynan qaysi mezonda kamchiligi bor? Ravonlik, lug‘at, grammatika yoki muloqotmi? Javobingizni o‘ylab, keyin tekshiramiz.
scenes.say: Do you prefer working alone or in a team? A: Team. Because team is good. B: Firstly, I prefer team. Secondly, team is important. In conclusion, team. C: It depends on the task, really. For anything creative I'd rather bounce ideas off other people, but when I need to concentrate, I'm far more productive on my own.
scenes.say_uz: Yolg‘iz ishlashni afzal ko‘rasizmi yoki jamoada? A: Jamoa. Chunki jamoa yaxshi. B: Birinchidan, jamoani afzal ko‘raman. Ikkinchidan, jamoa muhim. Xulosa, jamoa. C: Bu ishga bog‘liq. Ijodiy ishda boshqalar bilan fikr almashganni afzal ko‘raman, lekin diqqat kerak bo‘lsa, yolg‘iz ancha samaraliroqman.

scenes.title: Javoblar: C eng yuqori
board: A: too short, basic grammar (team is good)
B: mechanical linkers, repetition, no idea
C: nuanced, idiomatic (bounce ideas off), contrast
→ C = top level
scenes.say_native: To‘g‘ri javob C. A javobi juda qisqa va “team is good” kabi artiklsiz, sodda grammatika. B javobi uzunroq ko‘rinadi, lekin “firstly, secondly, in conclusion” mexanik, fikr esa yo‘q, so‘z takrorlanadi. C javobi esa nozik: “it depends” bilan boshlab, ikki holatni qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi, “bounce ideas off” idiomasi va “I’d rather” tuzilmasi tabiiy ishlatilgan.
scenes.say: C qualifies the question, contrasts two situations and sounds natural. B is organised but empty; A is simply too short.
scenes.say_uz: C savolga aniqlik kiritadi, ikki holatni solishtiradi va tabiiy eshitiladi. B tartibli, lekin bo‘sh; A esa juda qisqa.

scenes.title: Birinchi qism: suhbat
board: Answer + reason + example/contrast
2–4 sentences, not a speech
Personal, concrete, honest

examples.t: Not as much as I'd like to. I used to read a novel a week, but these days it's mostly articles on my phone.
examples.uz: Xohlaganimchalik emas. Ilgari haftada bitta roman o‘qirdim, hozir esa asosan telefonda maqolalar.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi qismda savollar oddiy: ish, o‘qish, qiziqishlar, kundalik hayot. Lekin oddiy savol sodda javob degani emas. Formula: javob, sabab, so‘ng misol yoki qarama-qarshilik. Ikki-to‘rt gap yetarli, nutq so‘zlamang. Misolga qarang: “used to” va “these days” orqali o‘tmish va hozir solishtirildi. Bu bitta gapda grammatik xilma-xillikni ko‘rsatadi.
scenes.say: Do you read much? Not as much as I'd like to. I used to get through a novel a week, but these days it's mostly articles on my phone.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘p o‘qiysizmi? Xohlaganimchalik emas. Ilgari haftada bitta romanni o‘qib tugatardim, hozir esa asosan telefonda maqolalar.

scenes.title: Xato: yodlangan javoblar
board: ✗ My hometown is Tashkent. It is the capital... (memorised)
✓ I'm from Tashkent, though I've lived in Bukhara for years.
Examiners may interrupt a memorised speech.
scenes.say_native: Ko‘pchilik birinchi qism uchun javoblarni oldindan yodlab oladi. Imtihonchi buni ohangdan darhol sezadi: matn tekis, tez, ma’nosiz pauzalarsiz o‘qiladi. Yodlangan javob savolga aniq javob bermaydi, imtihonchi esa uni to‘xtatib, boshqa savolga o‘tishi mumkin. Yaxshi strategiya: so‘z birikmalarini tayyorlang, lekin gaplarni yodlamang. Har safar jonli, savolning aynan o‘ziga javob bering.
scenes.say: Examiners can hear a memorised answer from the first sentence. Prepare phrases and ideas, never whole scripts.
scenes.say_uz: Imtihonchilar yodlangan javobni birinchi gapdan eshitadi. Iboralar va g‘oyalarni tayyorlang, hech qachon butun matnni emas.

scenes.title: Mock: birinchi qism
board: 1 What do you do in your free time?
2 Has the way you spend weekends changed?
3 Is there a skill you'd like to learn?
Formula: answer + reason + contrast
scenes.say_native: Mock imtihon boshlandi. Yozuvni yoqing. Uchta savolga ketma-ket javob bering, har biriga taxminan yigirma soniya. Formulani eslang: javob, sabab, misol yoki qarama-qarshilik. Ikkinchi savolda o‘tmish va hozirni solishtirish imkoniyati bor, uni qo‘ldan boy bermang. Pauza tugagach, namunalar bilan solishtiramiz.
scenes.say: Let's begin. What do you do in your free time? Has the way you spend your weekends changed over the years? Is there a skill you'd really like to learn?
scenes.say_uz: Boshlaymiz. Bo‘sh vaqtingizda nima qilasiz? Dam olish kunlarini o‘tkazishingiz yillar davomida o‘zgarganmi? Chindan o‘rganmoqchi bo‘lgan biror ko‘nikma bormi?

scenes.title: Namuna javoblar
board: 1 ...I'm a bit of a hiking enthusiast...
2 ...weekends used to revolve around...
3 ...I've always wanted to..., but never got round to it.
scenes.say_native: Namunalarni o‘z javobingiz bilan solishtiring. Birinchisida “a bit of a … enthusiast” kabi tabiiy ibora bor. Ikkinchisida “used to revolve around” va “now” orqali o‘zgarish ko‘rsatilgan. Uchinchisida “never got round to it” frazali fe’li ishlatilgan, bu britancha tabiiy ibora, amerikancha “get around to” deyiladi. Sizda shunday tafsilotlar bormidi?
scenes.say: I'm a bit of a hiking enthusiast. My weekends used to revolve around family visits; now they're about recharging. I've always wanted to learn the piano, but I've never got round to it.
scenes.say_uz: Men piyoda sayohatga ancha ishqibozman. Dam olish kunlarim ilgari qarindoshlarni ko‘rish atrofida aylanardi, hozir esa kuch yig‘ishga. Pianino o‘rganishni doim xohlaganman, lekin hech qo‘lim tegmadi.

scenes.title: Ikkinchi qism: yakka javob
board: 1 min prep: keywords only, not sentences
Structure: set the scene → story → reflection
Fill 2 minutes: end with WHY it matters
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi qismda sizga mavzu kartochkasi beriladi. Bir daqiqa tayyorgarlikda to‘liq gap yozmang, faqat kalit so‘zlar: kim, qayerda, nima bo‘ldi, nega muhim. Tuzilma: avval vaziyatni chizing, keyin voqeani ayting, oxirida mulohaza qiling. Aynan mulohaza qismi C2 darajani ko‘rsatadi: nima o‘rgandingiz, fikringiz qanday o‘zgardi.
scenes.say: Keywords, not sentences. Set the scene, tell the story, then reflect. The reflection is where you show depth.
scenes.say_uz: Gaplar emas, kalit so‘zlar. Vaziyatni chizing, voqeani ayting, so‘ng mulohaza qiling. Chuqurlik aynan mulohazada ko‘rinadi.

scenes.title: Namuna: yakka javob
board: Task: Describe a decision you found difficult.
Scene → story → reflection
had been weighing up / in hindsight / it dawned on me
scenes.say_native: Namuna yakka javobning boshlanishi va oxirini tinglang. Uchta bosqichni kuzating. “Had been weighing up” past perfect continuous orqali uzoq davom etgan ikkilanishni ko‘rsatadi. “In hindsight” va “it dawned on me” esa mulohaza uchun ajoyib iboralar. E’tibor bering, gapiruvchi voqeani shunchaki aytmaydi, undan xulosa chiqaradi.
scenes.say: A few years ago I had been weighing up two job offers for weeks. One was safe and well paid; the other was a small start-up with a lot of uncertainty. I eventually took the risk. In hindsight, it dawned on me that I hadn't really been choosing between jobs at all. I'd been choosing between two versions of myself.
scenes.say_uz: Bir necha yil oldin haftalab ikki ish taklifini o‘lchab yurgandim. Biri xavfsiz va yaxshi maoshli edi, ikkinchisi noaniqlik ko‘p bo‘lgan kichik startap. Oxiri tavakkal qildim. Ortga qarab tushundimki, aslida ishlar orasida emas, o‘zimning ikki xil ko‘rinishim orasida tanlov qilgan ekanman.

scenes.title: Mock: ikkinchi qism
board: Describe a time you changed your mind about something important.
You should say: what it was / why you changed / who influenced you
and explain how this affected you.
scenes.say_native: Endi sizning navbatingiz. Kartochkani o‘qing. Pauzada bir daqiqalik tayyorgarlikni boshlang: faqat kalit so‘zlar yozing. So‘ng darsni to‘xtatib, ikki daqiqa gapiring va yozib oling. Vaziyat, voqea va mulohaza tartibini saqlang. Oxirida albatta “how this affected you” qismiga yetib boring, aynan u eng ko‘p ball keltiradi.
scenes.say: Describe a time you changed your mind about something important: what it was, why you changed it, who influenced you, and how it affected you. Your minute starts now.
scenes.say_uz: Muhim narsa haqida fikringizni o‘zgartirgan vaqtni tasvirlang: nima edi, nega o‘zgardi, kim ta’sir qildi va bu sizga qanday ta’sir qildi. Bir daqiqangiz hozir boshlanadi.

scenes.title: Javob: namuna rejasi
board: Notes: university → medicine? → teacher's advice → switched to linguistics
Open: I used to be convinced that...
Close: Looking back, what struck me most was...
scenes.say_native: Bu yerda namunaviy qaydlarga qarang: bor-yo‘g‘i to‘rt-besh kalit so‘z. Ochilish uchun “I used to be convinced that” juda kuchli: u darhol o‘zgarishni bashorat qiladi. Yopilish uchun “Looking back, what struck me most was” kabi ajratib ko‘rsatuvchi, ya’ni cleft gapni ishlating. Agar ikki daqiqa tugamasdan gapingiz tugasa, mulohazani chuqurlashtiring: bu tajriba boshqa qarorlaringizga qanday ta’sir qildi?
scenes.say: I used to be convinced that medicine was the only respectable career. Looking back, what struck me most was how long I'd lived by someone else's idea of success.
scenes.say_uz: Ilgari tibbiyot yagona obro‘li kasb ekaniga ishonardim. Ortga qarasam, meni eng ko‘p hayratga solgani muvaffaqiyatning boshqa birovning tasavvuri bilan qancha yashaganim bo‘ldi.

scenes.title: Uchinchi qism: muhokama
board: Abstract questions: society, future, values
Speculate: It could well be that...
Evaluate: On balance, I'd argue...
Qualify: That's true up to a point, but...
scenes.say_native: Uchinchi qismda savollar shaxsiy emas, ijtimoiy bo‘ladi: jamiyat, kelajak, qadriyatlar. Bu yerda uch ko‘nikma kerak. Taxmin qilish: “It could well be that”. Baholash: “On balance, I’d argue”. Cheklash: “That’s true up to a point, but”. O‘zbek tilida biz ko‘pincha fikrni qat’iy aytamiz, inglizcha akademik muhokamada esa nozik cheklovlar yetuklik belgisi hisoblanadi.
scenes.say: Speculate, evaluate and qualify. At this level, absolute statements sound naive; careful ones sound intelligent.
scenes.say_uz: Taxmin qiling, baholang va cheklang. Bu darajada mutlaq gaplar sodda, ehtiyotkor gaplar esa aqlli eshitiladi.

scenes.title: Xato: kalka va ortiqcha qat’iylik
board: ✗ In my opinion, I think that...
✓ I'd argue that... / As I see it,...
✗ Everybody knows that technology destroys us.
✓ There's a case for saying technology...
scenes.say_native: Ikki tipik xato. Birinchisi: “In my opinion, I think”. Bu o‘zbekcha “menimcha, o‘ylaymanki” kalkasi, bir xil ma’no ikki marta aytiladi. Bittasini tanlang. Ikkinchisi: “Everybody knows that” kabi umumlashtirish. Bu argument emas, bu da’vo. O‘rniga “There’s a case for saying” yoki “Many would argue” deng: fikringizni himoya qilasiz, lekin boshqa qarashga ham joy qoldirasiz.
scenes.say: One opinion marker is enough. And there's a case for saying sounds far more convincing than everybody knows.
scenes.say_uz: Bitta fikr belgisi yetarli. There’s a case for saying iborasi everybody knows dan ancha ishonarli.

scenes.title: Tinglash 1: muhokama
board: Listening 1: Part 3 discussion
Topic: changing your mind in public life
scenes.say_native: Birinchi tinglash. Imtihonchi va nomzod o‘rtasidagi uchinchi qism muhokamasini eshitasiz. Nomzod qanday iboralar bilan taxmin qiladi, qanday cheklaydi, qanday baholaydi, shularga quloq soling. Keyin savollarga javob berasiz. Dialog qisqa, lekin zich: deyarli har bir gapda C2 darajadagi muhokama iborasi bor. Ularni sanab boring.
scenes.say: Examiner: Should politicians be praised or criticised for changing their minds? Candidate: Well, that's true up to a point, but it depends why they change. If it's in response to new evidence, I'd argue it's a sign of integrity. It could well be, though, that voters see it as weakness, partly because the media tends to frame any U-turn as a scandal. On balance, I'd rather have a leader who admits a mistake than one who digs in.
scenes.say_uz: Imtihonchi: Siyosatchilar fikrini o‘zgartirgani uchun maqtalishi kerakmi yoki tanqid qilinishi? Nomzod: Bu ma’lum darajada to‘g‘ri, lekin nima uchun o‘zgartirishiga bog‘liq. Agar yangi dalillarga javoban bo‘lsa, bu halollik belgisi deyman. Ehtimol, saylovchilar buni zaiflik deb ko‘radi, qisman chunki OAV har qanday burilishni janjal sifatida taqdim etadi. Umuman olganda, xatosini tan oladigan rahbarni o‘jarlik qiladigandan afzal ko‘raman.

scenes.title: Tinglash 1: savollar
board: 1 When does the candidate see changing your mind as positive?
2 Why might voters see it as weakness?
3 Which phrase does she use to give her final view?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savolga javob bering. Birinchisi: nomzod qachon fikr o‘zgartirishni ijobiy deb biladi? Ikkinchisi: nega saylovchilar buni zaiflik deb ko‘rishi mumkin? Uchinchisi: yakuniy fikrini qaysi ibora bilan beradi? Kerak bo‘lsa, dialogni qayta tinglang. Har bir javobni bir gap bilan yozing.
scenes.say: When is changing your mind positive? Why might voters see weakness? Which phrase introduces her final view?
scenes.say_uz: Fikr o‘zgartirish qachon ijobiy? Saylovchilar nega zaiflik ko‘rishi mumkin? Yakuniy fikrini qaysi ibora boshlaydi?

scenes.title: Tinglash 1: javoblar
board: 1 In response to new evidence → integrity
2 The media frames U-turns as scandals
3 On balance, I'd rather...
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: agar fikr yangi dalillarga javoban o‘zgarsa, bu halollik belgisi. Ikkinchi: chunki ommaviy axborot vositalari har qanday “U-turn”ni, ya’ni keskin burilishni janjal qilib ko‘rsatadi. Uchinchi: “On balance, I’d rather”. Diqqat qiling: nomzod uchta ko‘nikmani ham ishlatdi, cheklash, taxmin va baholash. Aynan shu muhokamani yuqori darajaga olib chiqadi.
scenes.say: New evidence means integrity; the media frames U-turns as scandals; and her verdict begins with on balance.
scenes.say_uz: Yangi dalil halollikni bildiradi; OAV burilishlarni janjal qiladi; xulosasi esa on balance bilan boshlanadi.

scenes.title: Mock: uchinchi qism
board: 1 Why do people find it hard to admit they were wrong?
2 Will social media make opinions more extreme in future?
Qualify → speculate → evaluate
scenes.say_native: Mock imtihonning uchinchi qismi. Ikki savolga javob bering, har biriga bir daqiqagacha. Uchta ko‘nikmani ataylab ishlating: cheklash, taxmin qilish va baholash. Ikkinchi savol kelajak haqida, shuning uchun “is likely to”, “may well” kabi ehtimollik iboralari juda o‘rinli. Yozuv davom etyapti, to‘xtatmang.
scenes.say: Why do people find it so hard to admit they were wrong? And will social media make opinions more extreme in the future?
scenes.say_uz: Nega odamlar xato qilganini tan olishga qiynaladi? Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar kelajakda fikrlarni yanada keskin qiladimi?

scenes.title: Namuna muhokama javobi
board: ...our identity gets tangled up with our opinions
...may well deepen divisions, unless...
...that said, it's also exposed people to...
scenes.say_native: Namuna bilan solishtiring. Birinchi javobda sabab chuqur ochilgan: fikr shaxsiyat bilan chalkashib ketadi, shuning uchun xatoni tan olish o‘zini yo‘qotishdek tuyuladi. Ikkinchi javobda “may well” bilan ehtiyotkor taxmin, “unless” bilan shart va “that said” bilan qarama-qarshi tomon berilgan. Javobingizda bu uch element bormidi? Yo‘q bo‘lsa, rejaga yozib qo‘ying.
scenes.say: I suspect our identity gets tangled up with our opinions. Social media may well deepen divisions unless platforms stop rewarding outrage. That said, it has also exposed people to views they'd never otherwise hear.
scenes.say_uz: Menimcha, shaxsiyatimiz fikrlarimiz bilan chalkashib ketadi. Platformalar g‘azabni rag‘batlantirishni to‘xtatmasa, ijtimoiy tarmoqlar bo‘linishni chuqurlashtirishi ehtimoli katta. Shunga qaramay, ular odamlarni aks holda eshitmaydigan qarashlar bilan tanishtirdi.

scenes.title: Hayajon: tanadagi jarayon
board: Nerves = adrenaline: fast heart, dry mouth, blank mind
1 Breathe in 4 — out 6, three times
2 Reframe: I'm not scared, I'm ready
3 Focus on the message, not on yourself
scenes.say_native: Endi hayajon haqida. Imtihon oldidan yurak tez urishi, og‘iz qurishi va miya “bo‘shab” qolishi tabiiy, bu adrenalin. Birinchi usul nafas: to‘rtgacha sanab oling, oltigacha sanab sekin chiqaring, uch marta. Ikkinchi usul: hayajonni qayta nomlang, “qo‘rqyapman” emas, “tayyorman, menda energiya bor” deng. Uchinchisi: o‘zingiz qanday eshitilishingizni emas, nimani tushuntirishingizni o‘ylang.
scenes.say: A racing heart is not a sign that you are unprepared. It is adrenaline, and it means you are ready. Breathe in for four, out for six.
scenes.say_uz: Tez urayotgan yurak tayyor emasligingiz belgisi emas. Bu adrenalin va u tayyor ekaningizni bildiradi. To‘rtgacha nafas oling, oltigacha chiqaring.

scenes.title: Vaqt yutish iboralari
board: That's an interesting question — I haven't really thought about it.
Let me put it this way...
How can I put this?
Sorry, could you rephrase that?
scenes.say_native: Miya bo‘shab qolganda jim turmang. Ona tilida so‘zlashuvchilar ham vaqt yutish uchun tayyor iboralardan foydalanadi. “That’s an interesting question, I haven’t really thought about it” sizga uch-to‘rt soniya beradi va tabiiy eshitiladi. Savolni tushunmasangiz, so‘rash mutlaqo me’yoriy: “Could you rephrase that?” Bu ball tushirmaydi, aksincha muloqot ko‘nikmasini ko‘rsatadi.
scenes.say: That's an interesting question; I haven't really thought about it before. Let me put it this way.
scenes.say_uz: Qiziq savol, bu haqda ilgari o‘ylamagan ekanman. Keling, shunday aytay.

scenes.title: Xato: kechirim so‘rash va jimlik
board: ✗ Sorry, my English is very bad.
✗ (10 seconds of silence)
✗ Eeeh... mmm... eeeh...
✓ Let me think about that for a second...
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek o‘quvchilari uchun xos uchta xato. Birinchisi, kamtarlik sababli “my English is bad” deb uzr so‘rash. Bu imtihonchining e’tiborini kamchilikka qaratadi, xolos. Ikkinchisi, uzoq jimlik: ravonlik bahosi tushadi. Uchinchisi, uzun “eee” tovushlari. Ularning o‘rniga to‘liq ibora ishlating. Ibora ham vaqt beradi, ham til ko‘rsatadi.
scenes.say: Never apologise for your English in an exam. Replace silence with a real phrase: let me think about that for a second.
scenes.say_uz: Imtihonda hech qachon ingliz tilingiz uchun uzr so‘ramang. Jimlikni haqiqiy ibora bilan almashtiring.

scenes.title: Tinglash 2: tiklanish
board: Listening 2: a candidate loses the thread
How does he recover?
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi tinglash. Nomzod gapning o‘rtasida fikrni yo‘qotib qo‘yadi. U qanday qilib o‘zini tiklaganini kuzating: qaysi iboralardan foydalanadi va oxirida fikrini qanday yakunlaydi. Bu ko‘nikma haqiqiy imtihonda sizni ko‘p marta qutqaradi. Uning ovozida vahima bormi yoki u xotirjammi, buni ham sezishga harakat qiling.
scenes.say: Examiner: Do you think working from home will become the norm? Candidate: Well, in some industries it already is, and... sorry, I've lost my train of thought. Let me come at it from a different angle. What I'm trying to say is that it depends on trust. Where managers trust their teams, remote work tends to thrive; where they don't, people end up being called back to the office.
scenes.say_uz: Imtihonchi: Uydan ishlash odatiy holga aylanadi deb o‘ylaysizmi? Nomzod: Ba’zi sohalarda allaqachon shunday, va... kechirasiz, fikrimning ipini yo‘qotdim. Boshqa tomondan yondashay. Aytmoqchi bo‘lganim, bu ishonchga bog‘liq. Rahbarlar jamoasiga ishonsa, masofaviy ish gullab-yashnaydi, ishonmasa, odamlar oxir-oqibat ofisga qaytariladi.

scenes.title: Tinglash 2: savollar
board: 1 Which phrase shows he lost his idea?
2 Which two phrases help him restart?
3 What is his main point?
scenes.say_native: Savollar. Birinchi: nomzod fikrini yo‘qotganini qaysi ibora bilan aytdi? Ikkinchi: qaysi ikki ibora unga qayta boshlashga yordam berdi? Uchinchi: uning asosiy fikri nima? Javoblarni yozib qo‘ying. Iboralarni aynan qanday eshitgan bo‘lsangiz, shunday yozing, chunki ularni keyin o‘z nutqingizda ishlatasiz.
scenes.say: Which phrase shows he lost his idea? Which two help him restart? What is his main point?
scenes.say_uz: Qaysi ibora fikrni yo‘qotganini bildiradi? Qaysi ikkitasi qayta boshlashga yordam beradi? Asosiy fikri nima?

scenes.title: Tinglash 2: javoblar
board: 1 I've lost my train of thought.
2 Let me come at it from a different angle. / What I'm trying to say is...
3 Remote work depends on trust.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “I’ve lost my train of thought”, ya’ni fikrimning ipini yo‘qotdim. Ikkinchi: “Let me come at it from a different angle” va “What I’m trying to say is”. Uchinchi: masofaviy ish ishonchga bog‘liq. Muhimi shundaki, nomzod fikrni yo‘qotishni yashirmadi, uni tabiiy tan oldi va hatto oldingisidan kuchliroq javob berdi.
scenes.say: I've lost my train of thought. Let me come at it from a different angle. Losing the thread is human; recovering is a skill.
scenes.say_uz: Fikrimning ipini yo‘qotdim. Boshqa tomondan yondashay. Ipni yo‘qotish insoniy, tiklanish esa ko‘nikma.

scenes.title: Vahimadan strategiyaga
board: 1 (silence) ...I don't know.
2 Sorry, I didn't understand nothing.
3 Eeeh... my English is bad, sorry.
Rewrite each as a calm, natural response.
scenes.say_native: Doskadagi uchta vahimali javobni xotirjam, tabiiy javobga aylantiring. Ikkinchisida grammatik xato ham bor, uni topib tuzating. Har biri uchun bugun o‘rgangan iboralardan foydalaning. Ovoz chiqarib ayting, chunki imtihonda ular yozilmaydi, aytiladi. Har biriga bir necha soniya yetarli.
scenes.say: Silence, then I don't know. Sorry, I didn't understand nothing. My English is bad, sorry. Fix all three.
scenes.say_uz: Jimlik, keyin bilmayman. Kechirasiz, hech narsa tushunmadim. Ingliz tilim yomon, kechirasiz. Uchalasini tuzating.

scenes.title: Javoblar: xotirjam variantlar
board: 1 I've never really considered that, but I suppose...
2 Sorry, I didn't quite catch that. (✗ didn't understand nothing)
3 Let me think about that for a moment...
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Birinchi: “I’ve never really considered that, but I suppose” va keyin har qanday taxmin. Bilmasangiz ham, fikr yuritish mumkin. Ikkinchi: “didn’t understand nothing” ikki inkor, standart ingliz tilida xato. To‘g‘risi “didn’t understand anything”, lekin tabiiyrog‘i “I didn’t quite catch that”. Uchinchi: uzr so‘ramasdan “Let me think about that for a moment”.
scenes.say: I've never really considered that, but I suppose it depends on age. Sorry, I didn't quite catch that. Let me think about that for a moment.
scenes.say_uz: Bu haqda hech o‘ylab ko‘rmagan ekanman, lekin menimcha, bu yoshga bog‘liq. Kechirasiz, yaxshi eshitmadim. Bir lahza o‘ylab ko‘ray.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: bo‘laklab gapirish
board: Speak in chunks: | Looking back | what struck me most | was how naive I'd been |
One key stress per chunk
Weak forms: was /wəz/, to /tə/, and /ən/
scenes.say_native: Hayajonda odam tezlashadi va so‘zlarni bir tekis aytadi. Yechim: fikr bo‘laklari bilan gapiring. Har bir bo‘lakda bitta asosiy urg‘u, bo‘laklar orasida qisqa pauza. Kuchsiz shakllarni saqlang: “was” gap ichida “wəz”, “to” — “tə”. Bo‘laklab gapirish ham talaffuzni yaxshilaydi, ham sizga nafas olish va o‘ylash uchun tabiiy vaqt beradi.
scenes.say: Looking BACK, what STRUCK me most was how NAIVE I'd been. Three chunks, three main stresses.
scenes.say_uz: Ortga qarasam, meni eng ko‘p hayratga solgani qanchalik sodda bo‘lganim edi. Uch bo‘lak, uchta asosiy urg‘u.

scenes.title: Bo‘laklarni belgilang
board: On balance I'd argue that the benefits of remote work outweigh the drawbacks for most office jobs
Mark the chunks | and the main stress in each.
scenes.say_native: Doskadagi uzun gapni bo‘laklarga ajrating va har bo‘lakdagi asosiy urg‘uli so‘zni belgilang. Keyin uni ovoz chiqarib, bo‘laklar orasida qisqa pauza bilan ayting. Kuchsiz so‘zlarni, ayniqsa “that”, “of” va “for” ni qisqa qoldiring. Esda tuting: bitta to‘g‘ri javob yo‘q, lekin bo‘lak ma’no birligi bo‘lishi kerak.
scenes.say: On balance I'd argue that the benefits of remote work outweigh the drawbacks for most office jobs.
scenes.say_uz: Umuman olganda, ko‘pchilik ofis ishlari uchun masofaviy ishning foydalari kamchiliklaridan ustun deyman.

scenes.title: Javob: bo‘laklar
board: | On BALance | I'd ARgue that | the BENefits of remote WORK | outWEIGH the DRAWbacks | for most OFfice jobs |
that /ðət/  of /əv/  for /fə/
scenes.say_native: Namunaviy bo‘linish doskada. “On balance” — urg‘u “BAL” bo‘g‘inida. “I’d argue that” — “AR”. Keyingi bo‘lakda ikki urg‘u bo‘lishi mumkin: “BENefits” va “WORK”. “outWEIGH” fe’lida urg‘u ikkinchi bo‘g‘inda, “DRAWbacks” otida esa birinchisida. “That” bu yerda bog‘lovchi, shuning uchun kuchsiz “ðət”.
scenes.say: On BALance, I'd ARgue that the BENefits of remote WORK outWEIGH the DRAWbacks for most OFfice jobs.
scenes.say_uz: Umuman olganda, ko‘pchilik ofis ishlari uchun masofaviy ishning foydalari kamchiliklaridan ustun deyman.

scenes.title: Yozuvni tinglash: baholash varag‘i
board: Listen 3 times: 1 overall  2 errors  3 strengths
Score each criterion 1–5
Note 3 exact quotes as evidence
scenes.say_native: Endi mock tugadi, eng foydali qism boshlanadi: o‘z-o‘zini baholash. Yozuvni uch marta tinglang. Birinchi marta umumiy taassurot uchun. Ikkinchi marta faqat xatolarni yozing. Uchinchi marta kuchli tomonlarni. Har bir mezonga birdan beshgacha ball qo‘ying va har bir ball uchun yozuvdan aniq iqtibos keltiring. Dalilsiz baho shunchaki his-tuyg‘u.
scenes.say: Listen three times: impression, errors, strengths. Support every score with a quotation.
scenes.say_uz: Uch marta tinglang: taassurot, xatolar, kuchli tomonlar. Har bir ballni iqtibos bilan asoslang.

scenes.title: Xatolar daftari va reja
board: Error log: what I said → correct form → type
Pick the 2 most frequent patterns
Plan: What? How? How often? How will I measure it?

examples.t: I said 'discuss about'; correct: 'discuss'; type: verb pattern.
examples.uz: Men “discuss about” dedim; to‘g‘risi “discuss”; turi: fe’l modeli.

scenes.say_native: Xatolarni daftarga uch ustunda yozing: nima dedim, to‘g‘risi qanday, xato turi. Masalan, artikl, zamon, fe’l modeli, talaffuz. Keyin eng ko‘p takrorlangan ikki turni tanlang. Hamma narsani birdan tuzatib bo‘lmaydi. Reja to‘rt savolga javob berishi kerak: nimani, qanday, qanchalik tez-tez va natijani qanday o‘lchayman.
scenes.say: What I said, the correct form, the type of error. Then pick the two patterns you repeat most.
scenes.say_uz: Nima dedim, to‘g‘ri shakl, xato turi. So‘ng eng ko‘p takrorlaydigan ikki modelni tanlang.

scenes.title: Xato: noaniq reja
board: ✗ I will practise speaking more.
✓ Every morning for 2 weeks I will answer one Part 3 question in 90 seconds, record it,
and count my article errors. Target: fewer than 2.
scenes.say_native: Eng ko‘p uchraydigan reja: “ko‘proq gapirishni mashq qilaman”. Bu reja emas, istak. Unda na vaqt, na usul, na o‘lchov bor. To‘g‘ri reja doskadagi kabi aniq: har kuni ertalab, ikki hafta davomida, bitta uchinchi qism savoliga to‘qson soniya javob, yozib olish va artikl xatolarini sanash. Maqsad: ikkitadan kam. Bunday rejani bajarganingizni yoki bajarmaganingizni aniq bilasiz.
scenes.say: I will practise more is a wish, not a plan. A plan has a time, a method and a number.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘proq mashq qilaman bu reja emas, istak. Rejada vaqt, usul va son bo‘ladi.

scenes.title: Rejani aniqlashtiring
board: 1 I want to sound more fluent.
2 I need better vocabulary.
3 My pronunciation should improve.
Make each one: what + how + how often + measure
scenes.say_native: Uchta noaniq maqsadni aniq rejaga aylantiring. Har biri uchun to‘rt elementni qo‘shing: nima, qanday usul bilan, qanchalik tez-tez va natijani qanday o‘lchaysiz. Bugungi darsdagi usullardan foydalaning: vaqt yutish iboralari, bo‘laklab gapirish, yozuvni tinglash.
scenes.say: I want to sound more fluent. I need better vocabulary. My pronunciation should improve. Make them measurable.
scenes.say_uz: Ravonroq eshitilmoqchiman. Yaxshiroq lug‘at kerak. Talaffuzim yaxshilanishi kerak. Ularni o‘lchanadigan qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: namuna rejalar
board: 1 3 recorded answers/day; count pauses over 3 sec; target ≤ 2
2 10 collocations/week from articles; use each in a recording
3 Shadow 1 min/day; compare stress with original
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Ravonlik uchun: kuniga uchta yozilgan javob, uch soniyadan uzun pauzalarni sanash, maqsad ikkitadan oshmasin. Lug‘at uchun: haftasiga maqolalardan o‘nta kollokatsiya, har birini yozuvda ishlatish. Talaffuz uchun: kuniga bir daqiqa shadowing, urg‘uni asl nusxa bilan solishtirish. E’tibor bering, har bir rejada son bor.
scenes.say: Three recordings a day. Ten collocations a week. One minute of shadowing daily. Every plan has a number.
scenes.say_uz: Kuniga uchta yozuv. Haftasiga o‘nta kollokatsiya. Har kuni bir daqiqa shadowing. Har rejada son bor.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq: to‘liq takror
board: Re-record Part 2 (2 min) using:
chunking + one recovery phrase + a reflection
Then score it again with your sheet.
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy ijodiy topshiriq. Ikkinchi qismdagi kartochkaga qayta javob bering, yana ikki daqiqa. Bu safar ataylab uch narsani qo‘shing: bo‘laklab gapirish, kerak bo‘lsa bitta tiklanish iborasi va kuchli mulohaza bilan yakun. So‘ng baholash varag‘ingiz bilan qayta baholang va ikki yozuvni solishtiring. Hatto bitta mezonda bir ball oshsa ham, bu haqiqiy taraqqiyot.
scenes.say: Record your long turn again: chunks, a recovery phrase if needed, and a real reflection. Then score it and compare.
scenes.say_uz: Yakka javobingizni qayta yozing: bo‘laklar, kerak bo‘lsa tiklanish iborasi va haqiqiy mulohaza. So‘ng baholang va solishtiring.

scenes.title: Dars xulosasi
board: 3 parts: interview → long turn → discussion
5 criteria: precision over showing off
Nerves: breathe 4–6, reframe, buying-time phrases
Plan: error log + what/how/how often/measure
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Gapirish imtihoni uch qismdan iborat va har birining o‘z strategiyasi bor. Eng yuqori daraja murakkab so‘zlar emas, aniqlik, tabiiylik va nozik fikr. Hayajonni nafas, qayta nomlash va vaqt yutish iboralari bilan boshqarasiz. Yozuvni dalil bilan baholaysiz va reja son bilan o‘lchanadi. Bugun siz haqiqiy imtihonning to‘liq mashqini bajardingiz.
scenes.say: Three parts, five criteria, three ways to manage nerves, one measurable plan. That is a full, honest rehearsal.
scenes.say_uz: Uch qism, besh mezon, hayajonni boshqarishning uch yo‘li, bitta o‘lchanadigan reja. Bu to‘liq, halol mashq.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Homework: complete the full speaking mock (all 3 parts, recorded)
Success: scores for 5 criteria with quotes + 2-point plan with numbers
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: to‘liq gapirish mock imtihonini yangi savollar bilan uchala qismda, to‘xtatmasdan yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: besh mezonning har biriga ball va yozuvdan iqtibos bilan dalil bo‘lsin, hamda eng ko‘p takrorlangan ikki xato bo‘yicha sonli reja tuzilgan bo‘lsin. Keyingi darsda yozish va o‘qish bo‘yicha to‘liq mock imtihon topshiramiz.
scenes.say: Complete the full speaking mock, recorded without stopping, then score it with evidence and write a two-point plan. Next time: writing and reading.
scenes.say_uz: To‘liq gapirish mock imtihonini to‘xtatmasdan yozib oling, dalil bilan baholang va ikki bandli reja yozing. Keyingi safar: yozish va o‘qish.

homework_uz: To‘liq gapirish mock imtihonini (uchala qism, yangi savollar bilan) to‘xtatmasdan yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: besh mezonning har biriga 1–5 ball qo‘yilgan va har bir ball yozuvdan aniq iqtibos bilan asoslangan; eng ko‘p takrorlangan ikki xato bo‘yicha “nima, qanday, qanchalik tez-tez, qanday o‘lchayman” savollariga javob beradigan sonli reja tuzilgan.

quiz.q: At the top level, what kind of hesitation is acceptable?
options: Pausing to search for basic words
quiz.why_uz: Eng yuqori darajada to‘xtash faqat fikr uchun bo‘ladi, so‘z qidirish uchun emas.

quiz.q: Which opening is the most natural?
options: In my opinion, I think that...
In my opinion I am thinking...
quiz.why_uz: “In my opinion, I think” o‘zbekcha “menimcha, o‘ylaymanki” kalkasi; bitta ibora yetarli.

options: Sorry, I didn't quite catch that.
quiz.why_uz: Standart inglizchada ikki inkor ishlatilmaydi; “didn’t quite catch that” tabiiy ibora.

quiz.q: What is the best use of the one-minute preparation in the long turn?
quiz.why_uz: Tayyorgarlikda faqat kalit so‘zlar yoziladi; to‘liq gaplar vaqtni yeydi va o‘qishga o‘xshaydi.

quiz.q: Is a strong Uzbek accent penalised at the top level?
quiz.why_uz: Aksent emas, tushunarlilik, urg‘u, ritm va ohang baholanadi.

quiz.q: Which phrase helps you recover after losing your idea?
options: I've lost my train of thought. Let me come at it from a different angle.
I don't know nothing about it.
quiz.why_uz: Fikrni yo‘qotganini xotirjam tan olib, boshqa tomondan qayta boshlash ijobiy baholanadi.

quiz.q: Which breathing pattern calms the body best?
quiz.why_uz: Nafas chiqarish olishdan uzunroq bo‘lsa, tana tinchlanadi.

quiz.q: Which is a measurable improvement plan?
options: For two weeks I'll record one answer daily and count pauses over three seconds.
quiz.why_uz: Aniq reja vaqt, usul, chastota va o‘lchovni o‘z ichiga oladi.

quiz.q: In 'the benefits outweigh the drawbacks', where is the stress in 'outweigh'?
Which sentence best qualifies a claim in Part 3?
options: Everybody knows social media is bad.
That's true up to a point, but it depends on how it's used.
quiz.why_uz: Uchinchi qismda da’voni cheklash yetuklik belgisi; mutlaq umumlashtirish sodda eshitiladi.
